question.problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨\,5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r,\,\text{_____}⟩,\,r\ge 0
$$

The vector-valued function $r(r,\theta )$ above parametrizes the half-cone defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${y}^{2}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}.$ What is the third component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
First, substituting

$$
x=5X,\,y=Z,\,z=3Y
$$

into our equation, we get the cone whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis:

$$
{Z}^{2}={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}
$$

In cylindrical polar coordinates, this cone has the equation

$$
Z=r.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,Z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=Z.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨5X,\,Z,\,3Y⟩ \\  & =⟨5\cdot r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r,3\cdot r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨5r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r,\,3r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $3r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
